title: Ebook v1
description: An e-book (Teracorp e-book factory, F4/EBK1 spec D2): one committed book per directory under ebooks/<id>/ -- ebook.yaml (this document) plus book.md, the book's canonical MARKDOWN SOURCE, which is the single source both renderers consume. Markdown is derived from the chapters below and the derivation is pinned byte-for-byte in both repos (kodemeio-dokploy deploys/tests/test_contracts_ebooks.py and the consumer's factory_ebook), so the prose a human reads in book.md and the data the factory renders from ebook.yaml can never drift apart. The block vocabulary is F3's (template.v1), shared BY REFERENCE as a pinned copy: heading, paragraph, list, table, image, spacer, footer, disclaimer -- a DRIFT test pins the eight branches to the template contract, and an unknown block matches no branch and is refused. The cover is a TYPED BLOCK SET, never free-form HTML: the book's own title/subtitle/author/locale metadata plus this document's `cover.logo` (an `asset:<key>` reference, because the licence lives with the asset and never with the document) and `cover.palette` (a KIT colour role name, never a hex value -- the brand kit supplies the colour). Two renderers are named as data, one per format: pdf -> typst, epub -> pandoc; a renderer the consumer does not have REFUSES by name ("typst not installed" / "pandoc not installed") and there is no fallback. The human label is `title`, not `name`: `name` is refused by the shared PII property-name denylist (deploys/tests/contracts_lib.py PII_NAMES), which every schema in this repo is checked against. The schema is deliberately SELF-CONTAINED (no $ref, not even to its own branches) so contracts_lib's schema walkers keep working on it -- at the cost of the block branches being written once here and once in template.v1.

id.description: Kebab slug; also the directory name under ebooks/ and the import key.

version.description: Monotonic per id: a consumer refuses a lower or equal version (drift refusal).

title.description: The book's title -- the H1 of the Markdown source and the cover's headline. Deliberately not `name` (see the schema description).

subtitle.description: Printed under the title on the cover and in the Markdown front matter. Optional.

author.description: The name printed on the cover. A pen name for a Teracorp imprint, never a customer: this is catalogue metadata, not personal data about a reader.

locale.description: The book's language, and the default render locale (`{{option.locale}}` overrides it per variant).

page.description: The page box of the PDF rendering, in millimetres. Kept for the EPUB book too (a reflowable book has no page box; the field is recorded, not a claim about the EPUB).

logo.description: The cover's logo, as a key into the consumer's licence-checked asset library. Never a URL: the licence lives with the asset, and the renderer places a LABELLED PLACEHOLDER for it rather than fetching bytes (spec section 4).

palette.description: The BRAND KIT colour role the cover band is painted with -- a name, never a hex value, so the kit stays the single source of the look. Defaults to `primary`.

cover.description: The cover as a TYPED BLOCK SET (spec D3), never free-form HTML: the cover page is built by the renderers from this book's title/subtitle/author metadata plus `logo` and `palette`.

id.description: The chapter's stable key (kebab slug), used by the factory's diagnostics and by any future per-chapter routing.

title.description: The chapter's heading in the Markdown source (an `##`), and its entry in the table of contents.

blocks.description: The chapter's content, in order, from the shared closed block vocabulary. Never free-form HTML.

items.description: A block. An unknown `type` matches no branch and is refused.

asset.description: A key into the consumer's licence-checked asset library. Never a URL.

chapters.description: The chapter tree: an ordered list of chapters, each a title and a block flow. At least one chapter must place a `disclaimer` block -- the kit's mandatory text is checked against the RENDERED book, and the structural half (a disclaimer block exists at all) is refused by the consumer otherwise.

key.description: Referenced from a block as {{var.<key>}}. A key starting with `child_` is refused by the shared PII denylist, on purpose: a book declares what it prints, never who reads it.

required.description: A required variable with no value refuses the render, naming it.

default.description: Used when no value is supplied. Must satisfy `type` (and `enum`).

items.description: A typed input. A value matching a PII pattern refuses the render's checks; a value for an undeclared key refuses the import.

additionalProperties.description: A key into the consumer's licence-checked asset library. Never a URL.

heading.description: A key into the consumer's licence-checked asset library. Never a URL.

body.description: A key into the consumer's licence-checked asset library. Never a URL.

fonts.description: Font roles (at least heading and body) -> `asset:<key>` of a usable font asset. A font may appear in this bucket and nowhere else.

additionalProperties.description: A key into the consumer's licence-checked asset library. Never a URL.

images.description: Image roles -> `asset:<key>` of a usable image asset. The cover's logo and every image block must appear here.

assets.description: role -> licensed asset key. `fonts` is the only bucket a font may appear in; `images` is the only bucket an image may appear in.

outputs.description: The formats this book ships. `pdf` is required (it is the expert-reviewed artifact); `epub` is the blueprint's second format and its absence must be an explicit, recorded choice on the work order -- the release predicate refuses a silent single-format release (spec D2/A5).

pdf.description: PDF through the Typst route. A consumer without the `typst` package REFUSES with the named error `typst not installed` -- never a fallback, never a partial document.

epub.description: EPUB through Pandoc, from the same Markdown source. A consumer without the `pandoc` binary REFUSES with the named error `pandoc not installed`.

renderers.description: format -> renderer. Two renderers, one per format, both honest about absence (spec D2).

kits.description: Brand kit codes this book is approved to render under. The kit supplies the palette, the fonts and the mandatory disclaimers, so one Markdown source renders many covers and themes, and a kit not listed here refuses the render by name.

renderers.description: A book that ships an EPUB names its EPUB renderer.
